steps.what: Distribute teaching materials, textbooks, workbooks, papers and pencils to students and resolve shortages

tasks.design: Retain physical distribution and shortage handling with the substitute. The existing lesson instructions in {DOCS} can identify materials, but they do not move books or pencils to students.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work is physical handling rather than a missing digital instruction.
tasks.enabler_now: No additional technology is needed for the unchanged distribution.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected class needs and missing or unsuitable materials.
tasks.human_edge: Notice who has not received what they need and find a practical substitute.
tasks.altitude: Distribution time and responsibility stay unchanged.

reach.task: Find an accessible alternative when a material is missing
reach.learn: Classroom storage and individual access needs

evidence.claim: Software instructions do not replace physical classroom material distribution in this design.

assumptions: Boundary is distributing already prepared materials, not buying, printing or planning them.
Regular teacher produces the existing material instructions outside this task; no extra structured inventory or pupil allocation input is requested.
All physical handling and shortage checks remain in s1. Native document access is sufficient; zero incremental upkeep because no new process or tool is added.
research_questions: How much distribution time depends on physical movement and individual assistance?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and net zero. No handling is transferred to students or assistants to create a saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach different subjects using the regular teacher's plan

steps.what: Read the regular teacher's lesson plan and clarify unfamiliar subject content
Teach English, mathematics, social studies or other subjects and respond to student understanding

tasks.design: Keep lesson understanding and subject teaching with the substitute using the existing {DOCS} or {LMS} plan. Generating another lesson is unnecessary when the work is to understand and deliver the regular teacher's sequence.
tasks.previous_blocker: The substitute must understand the supplied content and respond to an unfamiliar class.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing lesson access provides the teaching source; no new automation is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining unfamiliar material accurately and adapting to student responses.
tasks.human_edge: Maintain a useful lesson despite limited knowledge of the class.
tasks.altitude: Teaching time and authority stay unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify a difficult explanation in the supplied lesson
reach.learn: Subject concepts and the intended teaching sequence

evidence.claim: The substitute's own understanding and live teaching remain necessary even when lesson content is supplied electronically.

assumptions: Boundary includes substitute orientation and teaching, not the regular teacher's original lesson creation or formal marking.
Regular teacher produces the lesson plan before cover begins, under the unchanged handover process outside this denominator. Missing instructions require human clarification, not an invented plan.
s1 retains all reading and clarification time; no machine-generated subject answer is used. Native access is sufficient, and zero incremental upkeep follows from no new tool or content bank.
research_questions: What information is most often missing when the substitute first reads the supplied plan?

already_counted.description: Understand the lesson and teach responsively

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and net zero. Retain content understanding and all live instruction; no preparation time is transferred to the regular teacher.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Operate computers and audiovisual aids during presentations

steps.what: Find and open the specified presentation files or audiovisual resources
Connect and check classroom computers, display and audio equipment
Operate computers or audiovisual aids to supplement presentations and handle interruptions

tasks.design: Use native shortcuts to the existing lesson resources in {DOCS} and the presentation software category of {OTHER}. The substitute verifies the chosen resource, checks the equipment and controls playback during teaching.
tasks.previous_blocker: An unfamiliar classroom makes repeated file navigation slow, but shortcuts cannot connect cables or manage a live lesson.
tasks.enabler_now: Native links and a standard resource location reduce navigation without generating content.
tasks.still_hard: Access errors, incompatible equipment and pacing material for the class.
tasks.human_edge: Choose when to pause, explain or abandon a failed audiovisual resource.
tasks.altitude: Less resource navigation; equipment checks and live operation retain their time.

reach.task: Report a reproducible classroom playback failure
reach.learn: File access, output selection and basic fault isolation

evidence.claim: Native file shortcuts can reduce navigation while a teacher retains content checks and physical audiovisual operation.

assumptions: Boundary covers finding, opening, checking and operating existing resources, not generating the presentation or teaching the subject itself; overlapping live instruction must be allocated once in roll-ups.

Regular teacher already produces the lesson's file reference, version and intended sequence outside this task. No new structured lesson catalogue is demanded. Substitute verifies class, lesson, resource identity and access during s1's retained 21 hours.
If an existing reference is absent or broken, the substitute searches manually or asks staff; no tool guesses a file or opens an unverified resource to the class.
New shortcut and permission checks are charged below. Test native links before custom launch code; existing playback runtime earns no human saving.
Physical setup and live operation retain all 70 hours; no automation controls the class display unattended.
research_questions: Do existing resource links remove navigation time without increasing wrong-file openings?

already_counted.description: Verify resources, check equipment and operate presentations live

incremental.description: Check shortcuts and report access changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=21+25+45=91; gross 9 less upkeep 1 gives net 8. E1 scenario removes 30% of resource navigation only; missing references or already direct links may leave no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Counsel students about adjustment or academic problems

steps.what: Listen to students describing adjustment or academic problems and clarify immediate concerns
Counsel students within the temporary teaching role and involve the appropriate support professional when needed

tasks.design: Retain listening, supportive guidance and appropriate handoff with the substitute. Existing support procedures in {DOCS} define the route; no counselling chatbot or automated risk label is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: The substitute has limited history with the student and must recognise their role limits.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing school support routes remain available without new technology.
tasks.still_hard: Building trust quickly and deciding when to seek qualified support.
tasks.human_edge: Hear the student's concern sensitively and connect them to a responsible person.
tasks.altitude: Counselling time and safeguarding responsibilities remain unchanged; no clinical authority is added.

reach.task: Receive a factual concern handoff from temporary staff
reach.learn: Support routes, confidentiality and safeguarding boundaries

evidence.claim: Student support conversations need human listening and role-appropriate escalation; this design does not automate counselling.

assumptions: Boundary is temporary teacher listening, guidance and handoff, not specialist counselling or subsequent support delivery.
The student account is heard directly during s1 with all time retained. No structured risk score, automated triage, recording or emotion inference is used.
Missing background is addressed by an authorised human handoff, not a generated student profile. Native procedure access is sufficient.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new tool or data collection is introduced.
research_questions: Can substitutes identify the responsible support contact when a student needs help?

already_counted.description: Listen, provide supportive guidance and involve appropriate support

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and net zero. Retain listening, counselling and handoff; no saving is claimed from transferring support to another worker.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The substitute can find existing presentation resources faster while keeping material distribution, teaching and student support intact.
reach: Use the school's student-support handoff route
role.ambitious_version: A substitute who starts reliably with the supplied materials and spends classroom time teaching and supporting students.
